newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian miner hits back at Israel's Peres.
newsitem.headline: Australian miner hits back at Israel's Peres.

text.p: Jewish-Australian mining magnate Joseph Gutnick, criticised for funding new Jewish settlements in Hebron, hit back at former Israeli prime minister Shimon Peres on Wednesday, describing him as a sore loser.
Earlier this year Peres accused Gutnick and the ultra-orthodox Jewish Habad sect Gutnick belongs to of spreading "evil and hatred" by bankrolling settlement of occupied Arab lands.
Gutnick, 45, said after a speech to the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce that Peres was lashing out at him after his narrow upset loss to Benjamin Netanyahu in the May 1996 election.
"It was sour grapes," Gutnick told reporters when asked about Peres' comments.

Gutnick bankrolled Habad's campaign to help elect Netanyahu and the mining executive, who made a fortune from gold, has said he conceived the campaign slogan "Netanyahu is good for the Jews," which is credited as a key factor in Netanyahu's victory.
"He was very upset that he lost, that he's not prime minister, so he picked someone in Australia to let out his frustrations on," said Gutnick, an Orthodox rabbi who wears a long beard and skull cap.
Seventy-three-year-old Peres, who was succeeded as opposition leader by former army chief Ehud Barak earlier this month, attacked Gutnick and Habad in February,
"Gutnick -- he comes to pass out funds in order to argue, to spread evil and hatred, like all Habad now," Peres said.
Israeli-PLO peace talks have been frozen since Netanyahu began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
